players.name: Quentin Coleman
players.why: A shooter, rebounder and athlete who is already running a top-10 team's offense at 18. That production is why he's my No. 1.
players.off: Combo guard who shoots off the ball and now runs the offense.
players.def: Active guard who rebounds and gets steals.
players.swing: Running an offense full time. If the playmaking sticks, he holds No. 1.

players.name: Tyran Stokes
players.why: Biggest combination of size, strength and playmaking in the class, and every outlet has him No. 1. Coleman's production edges him for now.
players.off: Forward who brings it up and makes plays.
players.swing: Decision-making. The shot has shown up so far.

players.name: Jason Crowe Jr.
players.why: An 18-year-old who already shoots like this is rare. The passing is the bet.
players.off: Lead scorer who creates off the dribble.
players.swing: Passing. If he becomes a real point guard, he can push for No. 1.

players.name: Caleb Holt
players.why: Highest floor of the freshmen. The defense and rebounding translate on day one.
players.def: Guards the other team's best guard.
players.swing: The jumper. The free throws say it can come.

players.name: Bruce Branch III
players.why: The tools are top-3 level, but the free-throw shooting is already pushing him down.
players.def: Wing stopper because of his length.
players.swing: Free throws and catch-and-shoot threes. A 51% free-throw shooter rarely turns into a 38% NBA three-point shooter.

players.name: Jordan Smith Jr.
players.why: The outlets have him at 3, so this is my biggest fade. A 6'2" guard has to score efficiently to stay up top, and he hasn't yet.
players.def: Guards the other team's best guard.
players.swing: The jumper. He made 37% of his threes as a high school senior, so it's in there.

players.name: Ivan Kharchenkov
players.why: Most productive player on a top-10 team, and his defense was proven before the scoring arrived.
players.off: Wing who attacks closeouts and makes plays from the second side.
players.def: Guards the other team's best scorer.
players.swing: Three-point volume. If he stays at 40% on 5+ attempts, he's a lottery pick.

players.name: Amari Allen
players.why: Best decision-maker among the wings, and his shooting is real.
players.off: Wing who runs some offense and makes the right read.
players.swing: Creating his own shot. Today he wins with reads.

players.name: Alijah Arenas
players.why: Tools plus production. The outlets range from 7 to 58, so I'm betting on the version we're seeing now.
players.swing: Whether the efficiency holds once Big Ten play starts.

players.name: Braylon Mullins
players.why: Elite shooting on volume always gets drafted early, and he's doing it against good teams.
players.swing: Whether he can score inside the arc. Shooters who can't finish get capped.

players.name: Stefan Joksimovic
players.why: This is my biggest gap below the outlets. The talent is top 5, but I want production before I move him up.
players.swing: Shooting. Right now his free throws and threes are both below average.

players.name: Obinna Ekezie Jr.
players.why: A 7'2" rim protector who shoots is rare. The minutes keep him out of the top 10.
players.swing: Minutes. He needs 25 a night to prove he can carry this production.

players.name: Luigi Suigo
players.why: I have him here because of his size and the shooting potential.
players.off: Screener, roll man and occasional shooter.
players.swing: The three. A 7'3" shooter goes in the lottery.

players.name: Hugo Yimga-Moukouri
players.why: I'm betting on an athlete producing against pros at 18.
players.swing: The three. With it, he's a 3-and-D forward. Without it, he's a bench defender.

players.name: Tounde Yessoufou
players.why: He moved up on strength and his shooting jump. Outlets are still split from 13 to 57.
players.swing: Whether the jump to 44% from three holds over a full season.

players.name: Andrej Stojakovic
players.why: He's carrying a top-10 team as a scorer. His age and shooting keep him out of the lottery.
players.off: Slashing wing who creates his own shot and lives in the midrange.
players.swing: The three. Efficient volume as a lead option decides whether he's a first-rounder.

players.name: Caleb Gaskins
players.why: I'm betting on youth and tools. The efficiency has to show up by February.
players.def: Guards forwards and helps at the rim.
players.swing: Efficiency as a scorer.

players.name: Colben Landrew
players.why: He's built for the NBA and fits a role, but his shooting doesn't support a lottery pick yet.
players.off: Attacks closeouts and drives through contact.
players.def: Switches 2 through 4 and guards bigger wings.
players.swing: Corner three. If it hits 35%, he's a starter.

players.name: Brandon McCoy
players.why: His talent is lottery level. No college tape and a recent ACL tear drop him to the late first, not off the board.
players.swing: Whether he enters the 2027 draft at all.

players.name: Motiejus Krivas
players.why: His production is top 10, but a senior big who can't switch has a ceiling.
players.swing: Whether he can survive switches. In the NBA, guards will target him.

players.name: Thomas Haugh
players.why: He's ready to play now, but the senior cap keeps him behind the younger upside guys.
players.swing: Whether the three is real this time.

players.name: Ethan Brown
players.why: His production is real so far. The competition and sample keep him in the 20s.
players.swing: Keeping it up against Big Ten defenses and real length.

players.name: Miles Sadler
players.why: He's one of the best scorers on the board. His size and shooting keep him in the late 20s.
players.off: Lead guard scoring off the bounce.
players.swing: Pull-up three. Small guards have to shoot.

players.name: Billy Richmond III
players.why: His defense alone gets him drafted. If the shooting is real, he moves up.
players.off: Cutter and transition finisher who makes the quick pass.
players.swing: Whether the three-point shooting is real.

players.name: Dylan Mingo
players.why: His size and defensive tools are top-20 caliber. His shot is unknown, so he's not higher.
players.off: Secondary ball handler who pushes in transition.
players.def: Point-of-attack defender who jumps passing lanes.
players.swing: Whether he takes and makes threes.

players.name: Patrick Ngongba II
players.why: The numbers say lottery, the eye test says late first. The middle of the first round splits the difference.
players.off: Hub at the elbow and in the post.
players.swing: Staying healthy and holding up against real size.

players.name: Davis Fogle
players.why: His production and data are first-round level. His frame and shot need time.
players.swing: Adding strength so his drives hold up against NBA bodies.

players.name: Malachi Moreno
players.why: Young, efficient, and he passes. Bigs like that keep getting drafted in the first round.
players.off: Roll man and passer from the short roll.
players.swing: Strength. He has to hold position against NBA centers.

players.name: Daniel Jacobsen
players.why: 19 points on 76 TS% at 7'3" with 87% free throws. The outlets haven't caught up yet.
players.swing: Staying healthy for a full season.

players.name: Tyler Tanner
players.why: All-American production, but size and the cold start keep him out of the top 20.
players.swing: The three. Small guards have to shoot.

players.name: Anthony Thompson
players.why: His tools are lottery level. His production isn't yet.
players.off: Big shooter off movement and a mismatch scorer.
players.def: Uses his length on wings and forwards.
players.swing: Getting to 40%+ from the field and earning touches.

players.name: Miikka Muurinen
players.why: His archetype is coveted. His college production so far isn't.
players.def: Switches in space and helps at the rim.
players.swing: The three. His whole profile depends on it.

players.name: Alex Condon
players.why: His feel and passing are bankable. His age caps the upside.
players.def: Drops and shows on pick-and-rolls, with some switching.
players.swing: Strength. Can he hold position against NBA centers?

players.name: Matt Able
players.why: His shooting and size get him drafted. He needs more on-ball work to move up.
players.swing: Shooting off the dribble.

players.name: Matas Vokietaitis
players.why: He's productive, but traditional centers go late.
players.swing: A midrange or face-up jumper.

players.name: Najai Hines
players.why: His efficiency and size are real. Teams will want proof of his conditioning.
players.swing: Staying on the floor. That's both conditioning and fouls.

players.name: Dash Daniels
players.why: His defense translates. His creation and shooting are still question marks.
players.off: Secondary ball handler and spot-up shooter.
players.swing: Free-throw percentage, since it tends to predict whether the three is real.

players.name: Abdou Toure
players.why: He has upside, but his production is too thin for a first-round grade right now.
players.swing: His handle. Can he create, not just finish?

players.name: Sayon Keita
players.why: His tools are lottery level. His strength and polish are a year or two away.
players.swing: Adding 20 pounds without losing his bounce.

players.name: David Mirkovic
players.why: I'm ranking him on last year's production, and lower because of the injuries.
players.off: Point forward who also spaces the floor.
players.swing: Coming back and playing at last year's level.

players.name: JJ Andrews
players.why: He fits a role, but his early college numbers don't support where some outlets have him (B/R had him No. 9).
players.off: Downhill scorer who posts up smaller wings.
players.swing: Getting enough minutes to show what he did over the summer.

players.name: Klark Reithauser
players.why: His production in the youth leagues is first-round level. The injury is why he's not higher.
players.off: Big wing who shoots and runs some offense.
players.def: Active wing who gets into passing lanes.
players.swing: Getting healthy and playing pro minutes before the deadline to declare.

players.name: Trey McKenney
players.why: He's a real scorer. His playmaking decisions keep him out of the first round for now.
players.off: Scoring guard who attacks downhill and shoots off the catch.
players.swing: Running pick-and-roll without turning it over.

players.name: Pryce Sandfort
players.why: NBA teams always need shooting, and his is real. His age keeps him in the second-round range.
players.off: Shooting off screens and in handoffs.
players.swing: Whether he can defend well enough to stay on the floor.

players.name: Austin Goosby
players.why: I need to see the efficiency before I buy ESPN's ranking.
players.off: Plays both guard spots and pushes in transition.
players.swing: His jumper.

players.name: Maximo Adams
players.why: His rebounding and size are real. His efficiency needs to come up.
players.off: Score-first wing with a midrange game.
players.def: Guards bigger wings and crashes the glass.
players.swing: Turning his midrange game into threes.

players.name: Flory Bidunga
players.why: His athleticism and defensive resume are real. His height caps the ceiling.
players.swing: Switching onto guards, since his height means he has to.

players.name: Dame Sarr
players.why: His defense is a sure thing. His shooting decides whether he's a first-rounder.
players.def: Guards 1 through 4 and jumps passing lanes.
players.swing: Getting the three near 37%.

players.name: Cameron Williams
players.why: His tools are lottery level. In 10.8 minutes a game we haven't seen much yet.
players.off: Face-up four who spaces and runs the floor.
players.swing: Earning minutes on a deep Duke roster.

players.name: Pavle Backo
players.why: He's productive in a pro league, and his skill as a lefty big is real. His athleticism caps him.
players.off: Stretch five who posts up and passes out of the post.
players.swing: His defensive mobility.

players.name: Babatunde Oladotun
players.why: His upside is top 10. His production is nowhere near that yet.
players.off: Big wing who scores on jumpers.
players.swing: Strength. Can he hold his spots against college bodies?

players.name: Davion Thompson
players.why: His point guard skills are real right away. His size caps where he goes.
players.off: Runs the offense and shoots off the catch.
players.swing: Scoring off the dribble.

players.name: Shelton Henderson
players.why: His tools and production are first-round level. The shot isn't there yet.
players.off: Attacks downhill and plays some point forward.
players.swing: The jumper. Nothing else matters as much.

players.name: Paul McNeil
players.why: His shooting is real. The rest of his game is thin.
players.off: Shooting off movement and the catch.
players.swing: Scoring inside the arc.

players.name: Milan Momcilovic
players.why: His shooting gets him drafted. His defense keeps him in round two.
players.off: Stretch four who shoots threes and posts up mismatches.
players.swing: Finding a matchup he can guard in the NBA.

players.name: Jordan Scott
players.why: He's the classic 3-and-D archetype, with upside if he adds strength.
players.def: Rangy help defender who takes tough assignments.
players.swing: Scoring with the ball in his hands.

players.name: Cameron Houindo
players.why: He has the athleticism. He's too raw to rank higher.
players.swing: Developing any skill beyond the rim.

players.name: Amare Bynum
players.why: He's productive and efficient. His position is the question.
players.off: Rolling and cutting four, with some pick-and-pop.
players.def: Energetic four who protects the rim.
players.swing: Getting to 35% from three.

players.name: Massamba Diop
players.why: His mobility makes him a real prospect. His production and age keep him in the second round.
players.off: Roller and short-roll passer, with some pop.
players.swing: Strength, so he can hold up against NBA centers.

players.name: Rueben Chinyelu
players.why: His length and physicality are real. His age caps the upside.
players.swing: Showing he can switch and guard in space at the NBA level.

players.name: Alvaro Folgueiras
players.why: He has the skill. His athleticism keeps him in the second round.
players.swing: Holding up on defense against NBA fours.

players.name: Karter Knox
players.why: He has the athleticism. The shot isn't there.
players.swing: The corner three.

players.name: Cheickh Niang
players.why: He's young and athletic, with a real shot. He's still a project.
players.swing: Whether the three-point jump is real.

players.name: Christian Collins
players.why: He was a top-five recruit, but his injury means we've barely seen him.
players.swing: Getting healthy and earning minutes.

players.name: Bryson Howard
players.why: His recruiting profile is high. His freshman minutes are low.
players.swing: Earning minutes on Duke's deep roster.

players.name: Jeremy Fears Jr.
players.why: He's one of the best college point guards. His size and shooting cap his draft range.
players.off: Runs pick-and-roll and creates for others.
players.swing: Whether the shooting jump holds.

players.name: Johann Grünloh
players.why: His rim protection is real. His shot hasn't been there.
players.swing: The three. It decides whether he's a rotation big or a third center.

players.name: Stefan Vaaks
players.why: His size and skill fit the NBA. His shot hasn't been consistent enough yet.
players.off: Shoots off movement and runs some pick-and-roll.
players.swing: The three. If it's at 37% by March, he's a draft pick.

players.name: Moustapha Thiam
players.why: His tools are real, and his production has been inconsistent.
players.def: Rim protector who can play outside drop coverage.
players.swing: Finishing. He shot 68.9% at the rim last year.

players.name: Arafan Diane
players.why: He has the size and skill. In 12 minutes a night we haven't seen enough.
players.swing: Conditioning and mobility. He needs to play real minutes.

players.name: Jaxon Richardson
players.why: He has the athleticism. The shot is far away.
players.swing: The jumper. Nothing else matters as much.

players.name: Juke Harris
players.why: Last year was real. This year has been bad.
players.swing: Getting his efficiency back.

players.name: Deron Rippey Jr.
players.why: His recruiting profile is lottery level. His production isn't there yet.
players.off: Lead guard who attacks off the bounce.
players.swing: Earning minutes and scoring efficiently.

players.name: Cayden Boozer
players.why: He's a smart role player. His scoring keeps him low.
players.swing: Scoring enough to keep defenses honest.

players.name: John Blackwell
players.why: His scoring track record is real. His start at Duke is a red flag.
players.off: Scoring guard off movement and pull-ups.
players.swing: Getting back to his Wisconsin efficiency.

players.name: Nik Khamenia
players.why: It's a small sample, but a good one.
players.off: Connective forward who spaces the floor.
players.swing: Keeping the shooting going over a full season.

players.name: Neoklis Avdalas
players.why: His playmaking at his size is rare. His shooting and defense keep him low.
players.swing: The three.

players.name: Cole Cloer
players.why: I'm betting on the shooting reputation. The results haven't shown it yet.
players.swing: The shot.

players.name: Joseph Tugler
players.why: His defense is first-round level. His offense is second-round level at best.
players.def: Switches everything and protects the rim.
players.swing: Any kind of shot.

players.name: Roman Domon
players.why: He's productive with real skill. His shooting has to come back.
players.swing: Whether the three-point shot comes back.

players.name: Miles Byrd
players.why: His defensive profile is rare. His shooting has gone backward.
players.swing: The jumper.

players.name: Jacob Cofie
players.why: He has the athleticism. His production has gone backward.
players.off: Rolling four who also handles a bit.
players.swing: Shooting.

players.name: Nolan Winter
players.why: He's skilled and efficient, but his start has been rough.
players.off: Stretch big who scores from midrange.
players.swing: The three.

players.name: Nigel James
players.why: Last year's production gets him on the board, but his start has been bad.
players.off: Lead guard who gets downhill and creates.
players.swing: The jumper.

players.name: JT Toppin
players.why: His production is first-round level. The injury, his age and the missing jumper put him here.
players.def: Active four who protects the rim.
players.swing: Getting back to his old explosiveness after the ACL.

players.name: Adam Atamna
players.why: He's young, with a pro resume. He's here as a watchlist name.
players.swing: Earning real BBL or EuroCup minutes.

players.name: Killyan Toure
players.why: His defense gets him drafted. He'll have half a season to show his offense.
players.def: Guards the other team's best guard.
players.swing: His shooting when he returns.

players.name: Tomislav Ivisic
players.why: The skill is real. The age and defense put him at the bottom of the board.
players.off: Pick-and-pop center who shoots on volume and passes.
players.def: Drop big who struggles in space.
players.swing: Defending in space. If he can't guard pick-and-rolls, he's a two-way contract at best.
